brief: c267: about twenty panes light up across the town every night and there has never been anybody at one. windowLit() is the ONE pane predicate and LIT[] the register, repainted after applyLight because a warm pixel drawn before the multiply is slate by midnight. Put somebody at a window: a silhouette that appears, crosses the pane and goes — bounded per pane, on the pane's own phases from hash() and never R(), the way #177 gave the lamps their moths. A pane is a screen-space register and not a world point, so this is a different solve from the moths and you should say in the ledger which register you drew into and why. The observable is a night wide shot in which the block opposite is inhabited rather than stencilled.
successLooksLike: Over an evening, one or two of the ~20 lit panes have a figure in them at any moment and the rest are empty rooms; a filmstrip shows figures arriving and leaving rather than a fixed stencil; the daylight count is 0.00 and no night in a swept year is empty.
avoid: Do not add a second pane list — LIT[]/windowLit() is the one register, the way NIGHT_LAMPS became the one lamp list at #177, and a lit pane and an occupied pane must not be able to drift apart. Do not draw the figure into the ground or facade cache: it will arrive slate. Do not put a figure at every pane; a knot in one or two rooms reads, twenty identical silhouettes read as a pattern.
